messages:
natalie: quick heads-up: saw a reproduction locally where continuous coalescer kept stealing tiny requests during a KV warmup storm, pushing them into repeated reassembly cycles. p99 for tiny reqs jumped ~40ms.

ashley: ouch. are those tiny reqs being treated as normal-sized for eviction scoring?

ria: current logic scores by slot pressure + last_access. no token/size scaling. small requests often lose because they don't fill a batch, so the coalescer evicts them to prioritize filling slots.

mike: reminds me of the "starving smalls" pattern. We debated a token-weighted eviction before but shelved it. Maybe it's time to bring it back.

natalie: idea: token-weighted LRU where weight = max(1, ceil(tokens/64)). eviction uses weight-corrected recency score. lightweight to implement and preserves fairness for tiny ops.

ashley: weight is fine, but warmup affinity matters too. If a request will trigger many cold KV keys, letting it go first saves overall work. We should include an affinity hint field on admission.

ria: admission already has a freeform metadata map. We could add keys: prefetch_hint=kv_keys:5 and fastpath=true. no proto change strictly required, but makes it messier.

mike: can we try a hybrid: 1) quick pilot of token-weighted eviction + per-tenant micro-queue for tiny fastpath; 2) follow-up RFC to standardize prefetch_hint on the admission proto.

natalie: micro-queue semantics: small queue is assembled every X ms or when N requests collected (N small). it has slightly higher assembly priority but lower batching cap to avoid holding large batches.

ashley: sketch of admission checks: if tokens<=48 && tenant_fastpath_quota>0 -> tag FASTPATH -> route to micro-queue. micro-queue assembly threshold: 4 requests or 4ms.

ria: telemetry wishlist: fastpath_count, fastpath_drop_rate, fastpath_latency_p99, eviction_weighted_ratio, kv_prefetch_success_rate. need trace linkage between admission hint and warmup hits.

mike: ops: add a flag `--enable-token-weight-evict` and `--microqueue-fastpath` gated behind tenant flags. run canary on a subset of hosts.

natalie: small risk: micro-queue could amplify cost if many tenants spam tiny requests. mitigation: tenant quota + adaptive backoff that lowers fastpath grant when eviction_rate rises.

ashley: also make async prefetch mandatory for fastpath so we don't win assembly time but lose on kvcache miss. fastpath must trigger prefetch on placement signal.

ria: proto suggestion (if we standardize):
```
message AdmissionHint {
  optional int32 expected_kv_keys = 1; // soft signal
  optional bool fastpath_ok = 2;
}
```
Keep it optional for backward compat.

mike: Can we get a short experiment plan? metrics, KPIs, rollback criteria.

natalie: plan: enable on canary 10 hosts, 48h ramp. KPI: tiny-request p99 down >=25ms; global mean token cost increase <=3%; eviction storming not increase >2x. Rollback if KV miss rate increases >5% absolute or overall latency regresses for non-fastpath requests.

ashley: i'll open the canary patch with flags and telemetry. ria, can you add the metrics to the batcher dashboard? deploy-bot please make canary rollout ticket.

deploy-bot: ticket INF-5998 created: canary test for microqueue fastpath + token-weighted-evict. change list: batcher flags, metrics. ETA: 3d. :rocket:

ria: one last note: let's add unit tests for eviction ordering so we don't regress the weighting. small PR review checklist item.

natalie: agreed. thanks all — i'll draft the follow-up RFC with implementation details and the telemetry dashboard links.
